newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains ease on strong stg, despite drought.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains ease on strong stg, despite drought.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended easier as the effect of a stronger sterling won the battle against continued drought fears.
"People are still very concerned about the weather and not just domestically," one trader said, citing controls on water use in France and concerns in other European countries.

But the continued rise in sterling could not be ignored. Sterling climbed to fresh 4-1/2 year peaks after tearing through key psychological resistance at 2.80 marks on Friday, extending its assault on a generally feeble mark in Europe.
New crop continued to occupy the most attention on wheat, with November accounting for 289 of a total 700 lots traded.
November last traded 0.10 sterling lower, at 100.15 stg, having seen a high of 100.50 stg.
Shippers had been the most aggressive sellers, on new and old crop, the trader said. "But country merchants still wanted to buy the new crop," he said.
All the trade in barley was on new crop, with 30 of 53 lots on November, which last traded 0.25 stg lower at 97.00 stg.
